emotional stress in rats induced by "stick poking" over a lengthy period of 3 months produced experimental hypertension and changes in the morphology and morphometry of the mitochondrions of zona fasciculatas cells of the adrenal cortex.

the adrenal cortex morphological changes and the plasma corticosterone concentration in the rats subjected to long-term emotional stress.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

emotional stress induces an increase of corticosterone, which is a hypertensinogenic steroid in the plasma and also induces an increase of the number and size of mitochondria and lipid droplets in adrenal zona fascicula cells, which is a morphological change.
long-term emotional stress produces experimental hypertension and that the adrenal gland is involved in the pathogenesis of hypertension.

the adrenal zona fasciculta of rats subjected to emotional stress showed hypertrophy of mitochondrion and lipid droplets, and that this hypertrophy was associated with an increase of the corticosterone level in the plasma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
long-term emotional stress causes adrenal cortical hypertrophy and hyperfunction and induces hypertension.

the adrenal cortex of rats subjected to long-term emotional stress showed a significant enlargement of mitochondria and lipid droplets in zona fasciculatas cells, and that the plasma corticosterone level was significantly increased in the 3 months experimental group.
the adrenal zona fasci-culata cells are enlarged and hypertrophied, and the plasma corticosterone level is increased in the 3 month group, but not in the 1 year group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adrenal cortex of the rats exposed to the emotional stress showed morphological changes.

the morphological changes in the adrenal zona fasci-culata cell are not necessarily related to the increase in the plasma corticosterone concentration, which may be due to the fact that the adrenal cortex is a dynamic system that responds to stress by adjusting its function and morphology to the stress level and duration.
the adrenal gland is involved in hypertension induced by long-term emotional stress.
